recentItems.title: Explosion in northern Israel kills one and injures around 20 others
recentItems.description:
An explosion in northern Israel has killed a 15-year-old and injured around 20 others during a hiking trip organised by a religious school. Israeli authorities say preliminary findings suggest the blast was caused by unexploded ordnance, possibly after a student picked up or handled the device. The area had previously been declared safe for civilian access by Israeli authorities, raising questions about how the explosive device remained undetected. An investigation is underway, but officials have yet to establish exactly what happened. The explosion occurred near the border with Lebanon, where years of fighting between Israeli forces and Hezbollah have left extensive damage and unexploded munitions. There have been no reports of renewed attacks from Lebanon in recent days, suggesting the device may have been left behind during earlier hostilities. The incident comes as Israel prepares for parliamentary elections on October 27, with questions about security and military oversight likely to attract political attention. 

Al Jazeera's Nour Odeh reports from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank.

recentItems.title: Global energy sector under pressure | Talk to Al Jazeera
recentItems.description:
The head of the International Energy Agency (IEA) says we are facing the biggest energy crisis ever.

More than seven months on, it continues with little relief in sight. The US-Israel war on Iran is driving the crisis, which has disrupted global shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for 20 percent of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas.

That has sent fuel prices soaring, interrupted supply chains and raised fears of a serious energy shortage.

IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol says global oil stocks are declining fast. G7 countries and members of the IEA have tapped into their strategic emergency reserves. But relief has been short-lived and the global economy is still feeling the pain.

The Russia-Ukraine war is putting additional strain on the oil industry, as both countries target each other’s energy facilities.

Birol says if tensions in the Middle East are not resolved, it could have serious consequences for the world economy. He warns of challenging months ahead as winter approaches in the Northern Hemisphere.

Birol says it will take time for the energy sector to recover from this crisis, and he acknowledges the industry will likely never be the same again.

recentItems.title: Nepal floods: Oxfam warns communities fear more monsoon disasters
recentItems.description:
At least five people are missing in Nepal after a flash flood on Sunday.
A landslide blocked a river near the northern border, causing a torrent of water downstream. 
It damaged bridges, hydropower plants and dozens of houses.
Nepal is still recovering from devastating floods in August, along its border with China. 

Santosh Pandey is the Humanitarian and Disaster Risk Management Lead at Oxfam Nepal.
He says people there are concerned that more floods could be on the way.

Al Jazeera's correspondents, Obaida Hitto in Baniyas, Syria and Jack Hewson in Iraq's Anbar, report on this ambitious new overland corridor taking shape, with the potential to reshape the region’s energy landscape.

recentItems.title: Gaza: Still Reporting in the World’s Most Dangerous Places for Journalists | Witness Documentary
recentItems.description:
Maram Humaid spends her days reporting, writing and listening to the stories of Palestinians living through Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. When Israel orders the total clearance of Gaza City for the first time during the war, Maram goes through one of the most difficult periods of her life.

As she navigates motherhood, food scarcity and the deaths of colleagues, Maram continues documenting the war around her, aware of the risks that come with her work. Alongside her family, Maram moves through a city being evacuated. She meets Palestinians who have made the painful decision to leave and those who have made the impossible choice to stay.

Gaza: Still Reporting is a documentary film by Mohammed Sawwaf, Salah Al-Haw and Ibrahim Al-Otla.
